description: Stored exposure equals the number of days in the period (values 1-365) instead of years: the row length in days was written into the exposure column.
action_detail: Exposure recomputed from the period dates for every row of every policy, test and reference table as round((period_end - period_start + 1)/365, 4), the convention that reproduces the stored value on all unaffected rows (full 2023 year = 365 days = 1.0; full 2024 rows run 1 Jan-30 Dec = 365 days = 1.0). 114 training rows (motor 47, buildings 33, contents 34) changed from a day count to a year fraction; e.g. 365.0 -> 1.0. Flag column dq_flag_exposure_repaired marks them. The same recomputation was run on the three test files and on reference_policies: no test row differed from the date-derived value beyond 4-dp rounding, so no test value changed.
rationale: A row with exposure 365 would receive 365x the weight of a full-year policy in any exposure-offset model and would inflate burning-cost denominators (buildings 2023 exposure fell from 20,600 to 11,400 after repair). Dates are the primary record; exposure is derived.

description: Stored exposure computed on a 360-day year (value = days/360, 1.39% above the 365-day value), a second, distinct exposure defect alongside the day-count rows.
action_detail: Same recomputation as F-01 (exposure = round(days/365, 4)). 493 training rows (motor 206, buildings 121, contents 166) moved by -1.37% (e.g. 1.0139 -> 1.0). Identified as exposure == round(days/360, 4) and not a day count. No test row affected (checked).
rationale: A 1.4% exposure overstatement on 1% of rows is immaterial to level but it is a systematic basis error, not rounding; repairing all rows from dates removes both defects with one rule and leaves exposure exactly consistent with the dates used for claim linkage.

description: Buildings sum_insured recorded in a unit 1,000x too small (values 73m-568m CU against a market median of 229k-241k), present in training and test rows alike.
action_detail: sum_insured divided by 1,000 on 53 training rows and 104 test rows. Decision rule (same for train and test): sum_insured > 5,000,000 AND written_premium / sum_insured < 2e-4. Boundary evidence: the ratio value/median has no mass between 5x and 300x (largest legitimate value is 1.2m, smallest affected value 73m); on the affected rows premium/sum_insured is 1.0e-6 (median) against 1.03e-3 on normal rows, i.e. the premium was rated on the correct sum insured; other rows of the same policy carry values 1,000x smaller (median same-policy ratio 1,029). After division the affected rows' ratio to the median spans 0.25-2.4, inside the normal range. Flag column dq_flag_sum_insured_rescaled. Reference_policies checked: none affected.
rationale: A sum insured 1,000x too large on a test row would be extrapolated by any model that uses sum_insured (the main buildings severity driver); leaving training rows unrepaired would teach the model that absurd values are harmless. The premium ratio gives a per-row test that does not depend on a tuned threshold.

description: Contents sum_insured recorded 1,000x too large (values 7.6m-132m CU against a median of 36k), in training and test rows.
action_detail: sum_insured divided by 1,000 on 57 training rows and 135 test rows. Rule: sum_insured > 1,000,000 AND written_premium / sum_insured < 2e-4. Boundary: largest legitimate contents value is 283k (ratio 7.9x median) with a normal premium ratio; smallest affected value is 7.6m (ratio 212x) with premium ratio 1e-6 vs 3.3e-3 normal. Low values (5-7k, renters) were checked and kept: their premium ratios are 1.3-1.9x normal, consistent with a minimum premium, not a unit error. After division the affected rows span 0.21-3.7x the median.
rationale: Same reasoning as F-03; contents sum insured is the only size variable for the line.

description: Negative result: no other monetary column shows a power-of-ten cluster. written_premium (all lines, train and test), voluntary_excess, compulsory_excess, high_value_items and the claim amounts (paid, incurred, recoveries) have smooth distributions with no mass at x1000 or x0.001 of the typical level.
action_detail: Ratio-to-median histograms on log10 bins were tabulated for every amount column; claims amounts decline smoothly into the small-claim range (minimum paid 0.12 CU) with no isolated cluster; buildings written_premium has a genuine right tail (premiums 1,300-4,700 CU, 4% of rows) that is continuous, not a x10 copy of the main mode.
rationale: Recorded so the audit trail shows the check ran on every amount column and on the test files.

description: Negative result: no claim repeats another claim on (policy_id, peril, loss_date, paid, incurred, recoveries) under a different claim_id; no two claims even share (policy_id, peril, loss_date). claim_id is unique.
action_detail: Check run on the as-delivered claims table; nothing deduplicated.
rationale: A negative result is part of the audit trail (R-0002).

description: Claims whose loss_date precedes the first period_start of their policy (by 14-431 days; loss years 2021-2023) and therefore link to no policy row; their report lags (411-565 days) lie far outside the observed lag distribution (99.5th percentile 73-344 days by line), so they are date defects rather than late reports.
action_detail: 36 claims removed from the cleaned claims table (motor 28, buildings 3, contents 5; 35 closed, 1 open; net incurred 92,267 CU = 0.33% of the total). All other 9,222 claims link to exactly one policy row of the same line by loss_date (match rate 99.6% of claims); every claim's policy_id exists and its line matches the policy prefix. Shifting loss dates by +1 year would place 28 of the 36 inside cover but is unsupported by any other field, so it was not done.
rationale: The target is defined by loss_date inside the row period; a claim that cannot be attributed to any insured period cannot enter a row target, and leaving it in the cleaned table would put 2021-22 accident years into burning-cost histories. The same pattern exists in the developed market (414 of 163k claims, with the same long lags), so this is an operational artefact of the claims feed, not a sign that the emerging policies started earlier. Team to confirm whether these should be re-dated by the claims system or stay excluded.

description: Repudiated claims carry zero paid and zero incurred; they are kept in the cleaned table and contribute zero to any target.
action_detail: Kept as delivered. Other consistency checks passed on all claims: paid <= incurred everywhere; closed claims have paid == incurred; open claims have paid < incurred except 5 fully paid; recoveries never exceed incurred (net never negative); no negative amounts; report_date >= loss_date everywhere; recoveries occur only on motor own_damage (26% of claims) and theft (11%); third_party_id is present on exactly the bodily_injury and third_party_prop claims; repairer_id only on motor.
rationale: Confirms the target definition (net incurred, repudiated = 0) can be applied as written with no reinterpretation.

description: Latest loss_date 2024-12-29 and latest report_date 2024-12-30 are consistent with the stated valuation date of 31 Dec 2024; no claim falls in the 2025 test period. The latest accident year is incomplete: December 2024 shows 268 reported losses against a 2023 monthly mean of 385, and 20% (motor), 25% (buildings) and 12% (contents) of 2024 claims are still open.
action_detail: Nothing changed. Handed to target construction: the completion curve must carry the under-reporting of the last months (R-0106) and the open-claim adequacy of 2024 is examined under R-0105. The selector identifies the December-2024 losses, the month most affected.
rationale: Quantifies how much of 2024 is outstanding before any target is built.

description: Dominant large losses: claims whose net incurred exceeds 2% of their line and accident-year total. Buildings is driven by fire (top fire claims are 5.8% of the 2023 total and 9.7% of the 2024 total; fire is 6.6% of buildings claims but 45% of cost) and flood; contents by flood; motor by one open bodily-injury claim (2.0% of 2024).
action_detail: Not deleted. 27 claims listed (buildings 17, contents 9, motor 1). Handed to target construction for capping and redistribution (R-0104); excluded from the completion-curve weighting; mentioned wherever a buildings year-on-year comparison is made (2023 buildings burning cost is 68% above 2024 almost entirely because of eleven fire/flood claims).
rationale: With ~520 buildings claims a year, the top 1% of claims carries 27% of buildings cost; one claim moves a yearly level by 5-10%.

description: customers.occupation is free text with casing and whitespace variants: 80 distinct raw strings collapse to 40 after trimming and canonical casing, i.e. the 20 occupations used in the developed market plus a 'Self-employed <occupation>' variant of each (10% of customers).
action_detail: occupation rewritten as trimmed text with the first letter upper-case and the rest lower-case (the developed market's spelling, e.g. 'Care worker'); 'Self-employed ' prefix kept. 47,924 customer records changed; flag column dq_flag_occupation_normalised. Applies to test rows through the shared customers table. The schema mapping splits the result into occupation_base (20 values, common to both markets) and a self_employed indicator (emerging only).
rationale: Without normalisation a categorical encoder sees 'Retired', 'retired' and 'Retired ' as three levels and the test rows are spread across them at random.

description: Uniform ~12% missingness in 15 columns across customers (4), addresses (4), motor (3), buildings (2) and contents (2), in training and test alike, against 2.5% in the developed market. The null-count-per-row distribution matches independent 12% draws per column, and null rates do not vary by year, new-business flag or claim outcome: missing completely at random.
action_detail: Nulls kept as delivered (no imputation in the cleaned tables). Modelling tables carry them as explicit nulls / an 'unknown' level; missing-indicator features carry no information under MCAR and are not created. Sample of affected customer ids given; the full set is every row with a null in the listed columns.
rationale: Imputation would be a modelling choice, not a repair; a tree model handles nulls natively and a GLM takes a missing level. Recorded because the rate is five times the developed market's and reduces the effective sample of an already small market.

description: addresses.flood_zone is missing on 2.95% of addresses and the missingness is not at random: missing addresses sit lower (median elevation 4.4 m vs 7.6 m) and closer to rivers (1.15 km vs 2.4 km), i.e. they resemble flood zones 3-4 rather than zone 1.
action_detail: Kept null; in the modelling tables flood_zone null is a distinct 'unknown' level rather than being imputed to the mode (zone 1), because the missing group is riskier than the mode.
rationale: Imputing to the modal zone 1 would hide a flood-risk signal that the model can otherwise learn from the 'unknown' level and from elevation/distance_to_river.

description: customers.customer_since_year is a calendar time stamp: it equals period_year - renewal_count on every training and test row, the value 2025 occurs only for the acquired 2025 book (99,088 customers, 73% of the table) and never in training, so it separates train from test perfectly.
action_detail: Table unchanged. Excluded from the feature set; the relative quantity renewal_count (= tenure in years with the insurer, 0 for new business) carries the same information with the same meaning in every year and is kept.
rationale: A feature whose value identifies the year cannot transfer to the prediction year (R-0006).

description: renewal_decision records the outcome at the end of the policy period (renewed / lapsed / cancelled / mid_term_change / declined_by_insurer) and exists only in training tables; 88-100% of 'declined_by_insurer' rows have a claim in the period.
action_detail: Column kept in the cleaned tables (schema parity) and excluded from features. It is used only descriptively: mid_term_change rows identify the post-change rows that Part 1 found over-predicted (R-0309).
rationale: Not available at pricing time and partly determined by the claims it would predict.

description: customer_service_contacts grows mechanically with the number of claims in the row (motor mean 0.4 with no claim, 3.0 with one, 5.6 with two, 8.1 with three) and its upper tail exists only in training: values >= 5 occur on 2.8% of motor training rows and 0.01% of test rows; the test maximum is 5 against 20 in training.
action_detail: Column kept; excluded from the feature set. Selector marks the training rows with >= 3 contacts (the part of the distribution the test rows do not have). missed_payments_12m and days_quote_to_inception were tested the same way: their distributions agree between train and test and move only mildly with claims, so they are kept.
rationale: The contacts counted in a training row include those caused by its claims; in the test file the count is a pre-period snapshot. Same variable, different meaning (R-0005).

description: weather carries one row per address and calendar year including 2025, the prediction year; 2025 values differ systematically from 2023-24 (fewer hail days, more freezing days, less rain) and could not be known when the 2025 policies were priced.
action_detail: Table copied through unchanged. Year-specific weather is not used as a feature; if weather is used at all it is the address-level mean over 2023-2024 only. Part 1 found weather features hurt out-of-year performance (R-0302), so the baseline omits them.
rationale: Using 2025 weather would be future information on the test rows and would make validation on 2024 optimistic.

description: ncb_years exceeds years_licensed on 16% of motor training rows and 22% of test rows, almost entirely in the 17-24 and 25-34 driver bands (38-49% of those rows); a no-claims record cannot be longer than the licence. Neither field can be shown to be the wrong one.
action_detail: Both columns kept as delivered and used as delivered in train and test (the inconsistency is present identically in both). Sample of affected row ids given (first 1,000 of the training and test rows). The excess is 1-2 years for half the affected rows and up to 15 years.
rationale: Repairing either field would be a guess; the model sees the same joint distribution in test as in train. Flagged for the data owner because the test book (younger) is more affected than training.

description: expenses lists no comparison-site commission for the emerging market (null) although 5% of emerging policies in every line and year, training and test, come through the comparison_site channel.
action_detail: Nothing changed; the risk-cost target does not use expenses. Recorded for the premium build: a loading is needed for the comparison-site channel or the channel label is wrong.
rationale: A pricing report that loads commission by channel will have an undefined rate for 5% of the book.

description: discount_applied is a deterministic function of channel (direct = 0.05, broker = 0, comparison_site = 0 or 0.10) and the share of comparison-site rows with the 10% discount jumps from 14% in training to 77% in test: a change in commercial practice, not in risk.
action_detail: Columns kept. discount_applied is dropped from features as redundant with channel; channel itself is kept (its mix is identical in train and test: 70/25/5).
rationale: A feature that changes meaning between years would be read by the model as a risk effect.

description: Three motor repairers handle 80-83 claims each while the other 984 repairers handle a median of 5; the three concentrate 5% of all repaired motor claims with slightly higher average incurred (2,052 vs 1,862 CU).
action_detail: Nothing changed; repairer_id is a claim-level field and is not a pricing feature. Listed for the claims team (possible steering or network repairers).
rationale: Concentration is unusual against a flat distribution elsewhere, but it does not affect the policy-level target.

description: reference_policies holds 20 rows (7 motor, 7 buildings, 6 contents; 18 new business) that are exact copies of rows in the 2025 test files, in a wide combined schema with line-specific columns null for the other lines.
action_detail: Copied through with the same exposure recomputation and sum_insured rule as the test files (neither changed any of the 20 rows); the cleaned file carries the same dq_flag_ columns as the policy tables. Treated as the team's worked examples for the pricing report, not as extra training data.
rationale: Keeps the reference set consistent with the test rows it duplicates.

description: Full-year 2024 rows run 1 Jan-30 Dec 2024 (365 days, exposure 1.0) rather than to 31 Dec: the system books 365-day annual periods in the leap year, so there is no cover on 31 Dec 2024 for those rows (no claim has that loss date). 2023 and 2025 full-year rows end on 31 Dec.
action_detail: Nothing changed; recorded so that year-end filters and the completion-age calculation use period_end, not 31 Dec. The developed market has the same convention.
rationale: A naive 'period_end == 31 Dec' filter would drop every full-year 2024 row.
